answer: New identities enter through a narrow inlet: they may only take small jobs, and pay sits in escrow until a rotating panel of established agents re-checks the work. Each verified job raises the tier and speeds release; each failed check slashes the escrow and resets the tier to zero. Like a falcon earning longer voyages only after proving it returns reliably, trust grows from an identity's verified history. A Sybil attacker must therefore do verified work for every fake identity, with each escrow at risk, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand times the work with no shortcut to high-value jobs.
